articleTitle: Concepts Game Theory Applied in Smart Grid
abstract: The smart grid is conceived as a large-scale system that includes advanced power, communications, control and information technologies. To adapt these technologies, we must work on mathematical tools and solid techniques that can ensure the exchange of information, an efficient operation, improving in many cases the technical losses of energy and raise their indexes of quality and reliability, making the network capable of to solve any problem especially in the management of demand, customer management, decision making, energy exchange, energy storage, contingency plans, geo-referenced information systems, among others. In this context, this article presents an overview of the potential of applying game theory to address smart electric networks, providing a systematic treatment.

articleTitle: Technical Features in Solar Photovoltaic Mathematical Models
abstract: The world faces an environmental crisis known as global warming and carbon footprint, one of the main causes are the gases produced by the combustion of fossil fuels derived from oil. Faced with this panorama, different countries have looked for an alternative, finding answers in the so-called renewable energies, one of these possible solutions are in obtaining electricity from solar energy. These systems can be had in isolation or with connection to the electrical network. In this document we will therefore find a review of the mathematical models of solar panels and their various applications.

articleTitle: A Semidefinite Formulation of the Shifting Load Management
abstract: Demand-side management (DSM) has an important role in the optimization of energy utilization that aims to reduce the energy consumption and to increase the efficiency of the electrical distribution system. This paper presents a methodology for the optimization and control of shifting loads in a power distribution grid. A mixed integer non-linear programming model including variations on the spot price is presented. Moreover, a semidefinite relaxation is presented which allows to obtain a boundary of the problem. An integer solution is obtained by using a rounding algorithm. The paper has a threefold contribution: the use of group theory as a simple concept for designing algorithms, a general model which includes some stochastic behavior of the spot prices, and a semidefinite relaxation which can be solved efficiently. A numerical simulation in cvx/matlab complements the analysis and demonstrates the advantages of the proposed methodology to minimize customer electricity bills and reduce peak power demand.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Control System Using ETAP Real-Time on Generation Plant Emulation Using OPAL-RT
abstract: It has been notable the implementation of new generation systems based in non-conventional energy sources. Distributed generation and automation of the networks have been introduced on the electrical infrastructure. Currently the information systems play an important role for application of new solutions in monitoring and control of power systems. It is notable how the SCADA systems have been improved constantly in order to bring solutions for remote operation of the networks. The concept of State Estimation is part of the new features in SCADA systems, where it contributes for development of automation schemes and diagnostic of information systems. Engineers need real time simulation for implementation of new solutions in automation, monitoring and control systems. The present work describes the importance of real time simulation and how it is used for validation of the new automation schemes. An SCADA system using ETAP Real-Time allows to implement State Estimation, it is validated using real time simulation with OPAL-RT technologies, where it has been possible develop an equivalent model for emulation of the network.

articleTitle: Validating a Channel Model Propagation in Outdoors Scenarios by Using Bootstrap Method
abstract: This article presents the validation of a semi-empirical channel model propagation for outdoors scenarios in the frequency band of 2.4 GHz, with ZigBee technology by using bootstrap method. This model is estimated from the indicator of the strength of the signal received based on data captured in rural and suburban scenarios, in a range from 2 to 200 meters. Contrary to several articles of literature, we detected a discontinuity at 60 meters, we used linear regression to obtain the main features of channel model and validate the model with bootstrap technique. The results identify the main parameters of the model and we determine a correction factor in order to obtain a unique expression in both sections.

articleTitle: A Software Based on Eye Gazed to Evaluate Vowels in Children with Cerebral Palsy in Inclusive Education
abstract: Inclusive education have been promoted in public and private education centers in Ecuador. It's well known that teachers make his best effort to integrate students with disabilities in real classroom, but the vast majority don't count with assistive technology that guarantee a real communication with students with cerebral palsy. The evaluation process in children with cerebral palsy and speech difficulties, it's complicated because the teacher don't have a real feedback about the teaching process. In this paper, through the use of eye gazed technology, we present an educational software to be used in the pre-reading process to know the advanced of the students in the recognition of the vowels; children with cerebral palsy from 5 to 7 years old test the program and the result are presented here.

articleTitle: Glucose Detection Based on Low-Cost Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) Using Genetic Algorithm
abstract: The aim of this work is detecting glucose concentration based on low-cost electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) that works in a frequency range until 65 KHz through sine waves generated by a direct digital synthesizer (DDS). This system uses a pass band filter to reduce offset before a voltage to current converter which drives frequencies toward an electrode. This EIS employs a microcontroller capable of making simultaneous sampling to measure phase shift between two voltage signals. Three Cole-Cole model circuits were used to evaluate system performance. Besides, stainless-steel bipolar electrode was used to measure glucose at different concentrations in saline solutions, three circuits are proposed to model the systems as solution-electrode employing a constant phase element to approximate the polarization problem, a genetic algorithm was used to fit impedance modulus Z and phase . to the models, where a resistor and a RC circuit were the better approximation showing resistance changes due to glucose variations, which means electrical impedance spectroscopy could by one way to glucose detection.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability in Low-Voltage DC-Grids
abstract: This paper presents a general methodology for small signal stability analysis in low voltage de grids considering four type of terminals, namely: constant power, constant voltage, constant current and constant impedance. This methodology is useful for academic purposes but also in practical applications which includes dc-distribution and dc-microgrids. Simulation results demonstrated the proposed small signal model is accurate compared to dynamical simulations.

articleTitle: A New Methodology for Power Transformers Factory Drying Process Control
abstract: One of the most important phenomenon that increase the ageing of power transformers is the moisture accumulation in their oil-paper insulation system. The factory drying process of power transformers is made with the objective to reduce the moisture content present in the cellulosic insulation through the heat addition and control of variables as temperature and environmental humidity. However this kind of control implies to have an efficient method to establish the optimal drying times. In this work, a new methodology that considers the use of a coil's scale model to emulate the power transformer winding behavior using FDS measurement is described and a validation case is analyzed to assess the main properties of this proposal.

articleTitle: Non Linear Modeling for the Frequency Dispersive Effects and Electronic Mobility on Microwave Transistors
abstract: Differences between static and dynamic behavior of microwave transistors have been studied through different models. Behavioral models are very accurate for prediction of this phenomena without the necessity of electrical equivalent circuits. From other side, device level models based on semi-empirical equations can also model this phenomena by using non linear equivalent circuits but without the necessity of the knowledge of the physical parameters of the transistor. In this paper we will show the impact of the electrical mobility parameter in the prediction of the difference between static and dynamic behavior of microwave devices, establishing a link between this parameter and electrical equivalent circuits. Modeling and characterization of mobility for different transistors will be presented.

articleTitle: Obstacle Detection System to Improve Mobility of People with Visual Impairment
abstract: Visual information is one of the most important factors in the perception of the environment. People with Visual Impairment (VI) have many limitations to explore unfamiliar environments since they lack of vision. Previous works, carried out by other researchers, focus on helping people suffering from VI by using different technologies to improve environment percept, however, none of them analyzes the possibility of avoiding frontal obstacles at face height. That is why in thisarticle we propose a system for detecting obstacles in the superior frontal plane to improve the mobility of people with VI. The proposed system is based on ultrasound sensors and an Android application to process and communicate useful information. The system is low cost, wireless, ergonomic and user friendly. The results indicate that the system is capable of detecting (on average) 80% of frontal obstacles at face height. The implementation of the proposed system can improve the quality of life of people suffering from VI, providing independence in mobility in unfamiliar environments.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Nonlinear Regularized Observer for Neural Activity Reconstruction
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for neural activity reconstruction based on an adaptive non-linear regularized observer is proposed. The regularized observer is based on a discrete nonlinear state space system that describe homogeneous activity into the brain by considering a physiologically meaningful model. In order to obtain an adequately performance of the nonlinear state equation, the parameters of the non-linear model are also estimated by using a multivariate non-linear least squares estimator resulting in an adaptive non-linear observer. Considering the complexity of the model and the large amount of states to be estimated, an iterative solution of the non-linear adaptive observer is proposed based on an IRA-L2 representation with spatial basis. A comparison of the performance of the algorithm in terms of relative error is analyzed, and also the evolution of the parameters is considered. A simulation framework based on the solution of a continuous non-linear differential equation that describe the neural activity in each source is used to evaluate against the multiple sparse priors method.

articleTitle: Temperature Controller for a Nanoparticle Synthesis System
abstract: In this work, the implementation of a specific temperature control in a basic stirrer used as a nanoparticle synthesis system is presented. The control system was developed using a PID control. Stability and response time, was compared in both systems: with and without control, and simulated using Matlab. Results will be used as basis for the development of more robust control systems that help in the stability in synthesis temperature of nanoparticles and in the repeatability of the nanoparticles properties.

articleTitle: Diseño e Implementación de un Sistema de Control para un Electrolizador Alcalino
abstract: Nowadays, there are important efforts in order to reduce the carbon emissions originated for the human activities. Carbon emissions produced for internal combustion motors used in vehicles is one the main pollutant sources. An option in order to reduce this carbon emission is by means the use of hydrogen mixed with gasoline, this strategy allows obtain the same mechanical power in the motor with a less gasoline volume. Alkaline electrolyzers are a simple and cheap option to obtain hydrogen in order to be used mixed with fossil fuels in internal combustion motors. In this work a control system for a 100 W alkaline electrolyzer is designed. Experimental results obtained demonstrated a 92% efficiency of the power stage designed.

articleTitle: Wirtinger's Calculus for the Load Flow in Power Distribution Grids
abstract: This paper shows a Wirtinger's-Calculus based load-flow methodology for power distribution grids. This approach allows to obtain an algorithm which works directly on the complex domain maintaining some useful symmetries and a compact representation. The paper aims to introduce Wirtinger's Calculus as a suitable tool for power systems analysis; therefore, it is presented as a tutorial, playing especial attention on the implementation in modern scrip languages such as Matlab/Octave, which allow easy representation and fast complex-array calculations. A Newton's-based method is proposed in which the Jacobian is replaced by Wirtinger's derivatives obtaining a compact representation. Simulation results complement the analysis. Despite being a mature theory, Wirtinger's-Calculus has not been applied before in this type of problems.

articleTitle: Coordinated Operation of Multi-Terminal HVDC Grids Using Model Predictive Control
abstract: Multi-Terminal HVDC systems is one of the most promising technologies for large scale integration of electrical grids. The control of this type of systems is a challenging regulation problem with multiple inputs and multiple outputs. This paper presents a model predictive approach for this task where states are determined by a measurement as well as estimation when measurement is unavailable. Delay in communications as well as noise in the measurements are considered in the control. Simulations results on the CIGRE five terminals HVDC grid demonstrate the performance of the proposed control under different scenarios including N-1 contingencies in both the transmission lines and the communications.

articleTitle: Reliability and Flexibility Criteria to Locate Motor Operated Switches in Distribution Systems
abstract: Distribution systems traditionally did not involve much automation until the last quarter of the 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> century. The equipment installed on feeders was expected to function autonomously, with occasional manual setting changes. This was later referred to as `local intelligence' when other types of automation began to be developed. Recently, more stringent to improve reliability and efficiency of the power system and more automation has been introduced to distribution systems. In this paper, a general overview of structuring good criteria for switch location is going to be discussed. First, the definition of the optimal topology will be explained. Then, the criteria to define the right location of switches and its advantages on the distribution system is going to be discussed.

articleTitle: A Study of Spectrum Sensing Using an Experimental Platform for Cognitive Radios
abstract: Cognitive radio is a technology in which intelligent radios can change their parameters through software. The technology makes it possible for opportunistic users to occupy frequency bands allocated to licensed users that are not being used by these users for a certain period of time. A technique known as spectrum sensing can be employed in the search for these “free” frequency bands in a network. Therefore, spectrum sensing is one of the most essential characteristics of a cognitive radio to ensure that opportunist users do not interfere with licensed users. A number of theoretical studies have addressed spectrum sensing. In this work, a platform known as Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) is used to experimentally analyze the process of sensing the spectrum in actual scenarios, exploring its advantages and limitations.

articleTitle: Dispositivos SiC en Sistemas de Tracción Eléctrica, Análisis de Eficiencia en Inversores Trifásicos
abstract: The properties of silicon carbide devices (SiC) allow work in operation ranges greater than conventional silicon devices (Si) in applications, such as power converters for electric traction systems. Also, SiC devices characteristics open the possibility not only of working at a high switching frequency, and higher temperature range but also reduce the power converters losses. Accordingly, weight and cost of the cooling system can be reduced and the efficiency can be increased. This paper presents an analysis of efficiency between different power converters topologies used in electric traction system and based on silicon carbide devices. The analysis was developed by using simulations of different power converters topologies and realizing a comparison with silicon and silicon carbide devices at 100 kHz of switching frequency. In addition, the power losses for both devices technologies were studied for demonstrating the advantages of Silicon Carbide device in power systems for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: On the Use of Electrical Stimulation to Prevent the Loss of Muscle Strength During the Treatment of Fractures by Immobilization Splints
abstract: This paper explores the feasibility of using controlled electro stimulation in order to avoid muscular atrophy in an immobile limb during the treatment of a fractured or dislocated bone. The electro controlled stimulation is based on the use of electrodes within the splint which emit two waves that collide between them producing a stimulation to the muscle while the limb is totally immobilized by the use of a splint printed in 3D. As a result of the electro stimulation during the use of the splint, the loss of muscle mass in the limb is avoided.

articleTitle: System of Diagnostic for SiC Devices in Power Converts by Analisys of Curves of Lissajous
abstract: This paper present the analysis and implementation of a systems of diagnostic by images based upon the principle of curves of lissajous for Power Converter with SiC devices. The system proposed consist in a graphical interface that enables detect possible failures in SiC devices mounted on power converters using harmonic detection algorithms lissajous pattern and low AC supply to get a response in a graphic form of SiC device. Finally, the proposed system prototype is implemented to justify the validity of the analysis in different in different tests of SiC devices in Power Converters.

articleTitle: Estudio y Caracterización de Telas Conductivas Para uso en ECG Utilizando Procedimientos Analíticos
abstract: The present study was born from the search for materials capable of acquiring bioelectrical signals, specifically the electrocardiographic signal in patients who require constant monitoring. Currently disposable Ag/AgCl adhesive electrodes are widely used which attach to the patient's skin and capture the bioelectrical signal to the biomedical recording and processing device. Although the signal acquisition by means of these electrodes is functional, they generate discomfort or pain when coupled to the skin. Because of this, we are studying the possibility of replacing conventional electrodes in exchange for a conductive fabric that is integrated into a garment that fits the patient's body. This work consists of measuring the conductive fabric (Conductive fabrics Shieldex) finding values of resistance and continuity, with these data are performed analytical procedures to determine if it is feasible to use the conductive fabric in exchange for the adhesive electrodes, as well as to establish how reliable is the use of this fabric to conduct the ECG signal from the body of the patient to an electronic system of a wearable monitoring that will be developed in a later phase.

articleTitle: Proposal for Advanced Metering Infrastructure in Distribution Systems with Generation Distributed in Low Voltage Electrical Networks
abstract: As part of the research work of the GISEL group of the UIS, the need to build a state of the art on the Advanced Measurement Infrastructure (AMI, its acronym in English) and its application in distribution systems with distributed generation and in the Building was identified of Electrical Engineering. In this sense, this work of degree compiled and synthesized information according to the needs (mainly) of the GISEL group of the UIS in being at the forefront in technologies that promote the efficient use of electric power. Initially, several architectures of AMI systems are presented in the literature with the purpose of knowing similarities, differences and challenges in the application. Then, 4 barriers commonly found in the literature were identified (investment, hourly pricing, information security and user acceptance) that could delay the implementation of AMI systems; and the information was contextualized to the current situation in Colombia. Subsequently, an electrical system with the integration of FNCER (particularly photovoltaic systems) on a small scale and the characteristics of intelligent measurement for such a point of connection in low voltage are specified, starting from information on legislation, regulations, resolutions and decrees in Colombia. Likewise, an AMI system is proposed in a low voltage network with integration of photovoltaic generation.

articleTitle: Measurements and Analysis of I/Q Signal Using Software Defined Radio for Evaluation of Technical Operational Quality of Digital Television ISDB-T
abstract: In the present article, we will use a tool based on Software Defined Radio (SDR) [1] and USRP (Universal Serial Radio Peripheral) N200 [2] to measure I/Q imbalance impairments such as Amplitude Imbalance, Quadrature Error as well as Residual Carrier, which get worse the quality of the digital television base band signal. These parameters evaluate the performance of a Digital Television modulator [11]. Moreover, we will also measure the Signal-to-Noise Ratio and the Modulation Error Ratio, the latter will provide a single “figure of merit” analysis of the received signal in order to summary all impairments present from transmitter to receiver.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Photovoltaic Scan Circuit for Global Maximum Power Point Tracking
abstract: This paper presents the partial shading effect on a solar photovoltaic system and proposes a circuit for scanning the power-voltage curve. In the first part of this document the partial shading effect is presented, then an experimental set-up is shown where a simple Perturb & Observe algorithm is trapped in a local point of maximum power. The next part gives design guidelines for the electronic board implementation and finally the experimental results with different power and shadow conditions are presented.

articleTitle: Characterization in Medium Voltage Stator Coils Using Dielectric Frequency Domain Spectroscopy
abstract: The Dielectric Frequency Domain Spectroscopy (FDS) is a widely used test to estimate the moisture content in power transformers. However, this diagnostic technique has potential to be utilized in different applications where the moisture level estimation is a critical parameter. In this paper, the FDS has been tested for moisture characterization in stator-winding coils. The main idea is being able to evaluate the moisture content during stator winding coil manufacturing. The laboratory test described in this paper has been carried out by moistened and de-moistened controlled laboratory tests, using FDS sweeps and measuring the moisture content by the coil weight.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Induction Motors Considering the Saturation Effect Applying the Finite Element Method
abstract: Three-phase induction motors are the most used motors in the industrial sector. The magnetic saturation phenomenon is always present in its operation, however, it is not usually included in the performance analisis due to complexity. This paper present a methodology to introduce the magnetic saturation in the electromagnetic field equations, then the equations are solved applying the Finite Element Method (FEM). The methodology allows the transient analysis of the induction motor considering the phenomenon of magnetic saturation, observing that the magnetic saturation introduces oscillations in the transient characteristics of the current and the electromagnetic torque due to the deformation of the waveform of the magnetic field.

articleTitle: New Approach to Develop Knowledge-Based System for Environmental Conflicts Analysis Using Fuzzy Logic and Grey Systems
abstract: The analysis of environmental conflicts is of vital importance to verify the viability and analyze the impact of projects in environments with a social presence The grey systems facilitate the obtaining of knowledge in environments that are not very clear or with little information and the diffuse logic allows through linguistic variables and fuzzy sets to represent the conceptual knowledge in the computer and the IF-THEN rules allow to make the inference based on those concepts and give conceptual results easily accessible to people. In this paper we propose a approach to develop systems based on knowledge using grey systems and fuzzy logic for analysis of environmental conflicts during all phases of projects A test is carried out using the case study data in [1] of a mining project in northern Peru and a knowledge-based system that can be used for the analysis of environmental conflicts during all phases of the project or for analysis in environments with similar characteristics is implemented.

articleTitle: A Methodology for the Identification of Design Faults in a Prototype of a Medium Power Three-Phase Inverter
abstract: This document describes a methodology for identification of design errors in a two-level three-phase inverter prototype, with a 500VA/60Hz transformer for coupling to the power grid. The designed three-phase inverter, under test, uses a six IGBTs' bridge as main power switching elements, three single-phase transformers for coupling to the 220Vac/1KVA grid, measurement cards, trip control for the IGBTs and protection circuits. The methodology employed for this converter can be applied to industrial inverters of small and medium power.

articleTitle: Strategies of Environmental Management to Eliminate the Carbon Footprint Generated by the use of Conventional Energies in a Hospital Institution Level 4
abstract: It is intended to evaluate the environmental impact generated by the use of conventional energy in a hospital level 4, and the mitigation obtained with the implementation of a photovoltaic system. The above taking into account that, in order to guarantee compliance with health services, the institutions can use different conventional and some renewable energy sources from the country's electricity grid. In this study, the institution supplements its high daily energy demands using mains electricity and steam boilers. The latter contribute to worsen environmental health problems by emitting greenhouse gases (determined in tonnes of CO2 equivalent) daily into the environment. As a possible solution to the above problem, the specific and overall energy demands of the institution are analyzed. With this information, the carbon footprint, through ISO 14064-1, will be calculated over a period of one year, identifying the direct and indirect sources and their respective emissions. Subsequently, environmental management strategies were established to mitigate the carbon footprint generated. As a result, we identify and present in this article, the co-benefits for the implementation of a solar photovoltaic system, considering national and international regulations.

articleTitle: Analysis Power Quality of a Photovoltaic System Connected to the Grid-Tie
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: photovoltaic power systems; distributed power generation; power grids; power engineering computing; optimisation; invertors; renewable energy sources; power convertors; induction motors; power generation economics.

articleTitle: Multi-Parametric Analysis of Stator Faults on Three-Phase Squirrel Cage Induction Motors
abstract: Present paper explores the multi-parametric analysis as a tool for online diagnosis of statoric electric faults in three-phase squirrel cage induction motors. A set of five characteristic parameters commonly used for diagnostic purposes are calculated, analyzed and compared to identify their possible usability in low voltage and low power motors. Five different operating motors ranged from 6-20hp/220V are used as a base of comparison. Some of the motors analyzed are actually failed but some others are in good condition and exhibit an unusual value for some of the described parameters. The evidence indicates that the analysis of just one failure parameter or the application of only one diagnosis technique result in an erroneous diagnosis.

articleTitle: Assessment of Uncertainty Effects in Integrated Generation and Transmission Expansion Planning: A Colombian Case Study
abstract: In this paper a set of hydrological, demand growth and fuel cost scenarios are constructed in order to analyze its impacts over long-term integrated transmission and generation planning (ITGP) in Colombia. This ITGP is a co-optimization based tool that makes the most cost-efficient solution in terms of transmission and generation considering security-related constraints as well as detailed hydro-thermal-renewable operating conditions on a yearly basis. This kind of tools are necessary in the Colombian context since the construction of new transmission projects is becoming more difficult due to environmental; thus, candidate transmission and generation projects compete each other in the co-optimization model in order to satisfy energy demand as well as guaranteeing cost-efficiency and high security and reliability levels. Finally, nine scenarios are carefully analyzed and evaluated in order to identify the most critical conditions for the operation of the power system under study.

articleTitle: Traffic Model for Narrow Band Power Line Communications Networks
abstract: Today, Internet of Things is an important topic in Research. One key technology for IoT development is PLC (Power Line Communications), which is widely used in Domotic Networks. Although PLC for low voltage networks have been studied widely in physical layer aspects, one important theorical lack of this studies is the abscence of traffic models for these networks. Then, there are no models that allows dimentioning in such scenarios. With the aim to improve this situation, we have performed a study with a Narrow Band PLC Low Voltage Network. In this work, we have performed traffic measurements, and we obtained that this system can be modeled as a Poisson traffic model, which allows PLC networks dimentioning in a simple way.

articleTitle: A Loop Shaping Control Strategy for Boost-Inverter Topology Applied to Wind Turbine Generators
abstract: This paper presents a Loop shaping controller based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> for a full power conversion system. The system is based on permanent magnet synchronous wind generator and a Boost-Inverter topology in order to supply the generated energy in the grid. This controller is designed to reduce the low and mid frequency ripples generated by the wind turbine speed and the 3-phase inverter respectively. Results demonstrate adequate performance and the fulfillment of control objectives.

articleTitle: Design and Automation of Atmospheric Binary Distillation Unit for Water and Ethanol
abstract: Distillation is one of the core processes in some sectors of the industry, such as petrochemicals, food, pharmaceuticals and others. One of the main characteristics of distillation is the ability to allow the separation of components through heating processes, to extract valuable products used in the different fields of the economy. The purpose of this work is the modeling and design of a binary distillation unit at the laboratory level, modular, compact, versatile and automated, integrating the control and supervision of the process through a friendly and reliable platform, within a controlled and safe environment. Among the results obtained from this project are the simulation in MATLAB and the design of the pilot distillation unit.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Geometric Modification in Savonius Rotor Using CFD Evaluación de Modificación Geométrica en Rotor Savonius Usando CFD
abstract: In Colombia, there are areas not connected to the national electricity grid because of different socioeconomic factors, establishing territories under conditions of vulnerability. In this sense, any initiative aiming to solve this growing situation is imperative. Savonius rotors have been widely implemented and studied due to their numerous advantages for small-scale generation. The investigation of this type of rotors as well as the implementation of geometric changes with the aim of improving their efficiency, are potentially feasible solutions to provide electricity to off-grid populations from the national network in remote areas of the country. Therefore, the study of a Savonius rotor and the analysis of a modified geometry was made using CFD in a 2D domain. The SST model k-ω was selected for a turbulent flow condition. As a result, an alternate configuration is proposed that could potentially achieve higher yields at low TSRs.

articleTitle: Optimization of Distribution Transformers Using Gams
abstract: The article synthesizes the most relevant results of the research work related to the formulation of an optimization model for distribution transformers with application in the planning and design stages of the distribution networks, which considers technical and economic aspects, whose resolution is through GAMS (General Algebraic Modeling System)

articleTitle: Analysis and Modeling of Temperature Control for the Crude Mill of a Cement Plant: An Industrial Case Study Involving PID Control
abstract: This work presents an application of knowledge in the field of automatic control to a real process, it is intended to stabilize the drying process of the crude mill of the cement manufacturing process of the Guapán industrial plant of the Cementera Union Company. The main objective of this study is the analysis and modeling of a resources that the plant currently has and the proposed a retune of the PID controllers. This system is realized using a model following PID controller design approach and the results from simulation studies are presented, which demonstrate the level of accuracy for the engineering process.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Induction Machines Considering the Effect of Magnetic Saturation Using Spatial Vectors Method
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for modeling and simulation of three-phase induction machine in transient state, including the effect of magnetic saturation. The spatial vector method is used for the modeling of this machine, which makes it possible to simplify the non-linear differential equations with variable coefficients. The developed methodology is applied to analyze the start-up process of an induction machine for different loads, comparing the linear model without saturation with the proposed model.

articleTitle: Device for the Treatment of Hydrocephalus: Experimental Protocol in an Animal Model
abstract: After the development of a new implantable technology for the treatment of hydrocephalus that presents competitive advantages at the reprogramming process and could detect obstructions, providing information to the specialist on the intracranial pressure of the patient and some data of the system condition, it is necessary to advance in the preliminary tests, evaluating the efficacy and safety of the new device in an animal model, for which the following paper presents an experimental protocol. The result is the methodology of a randomized controlled trial of noninferiority in dogs suffering from this disease and that require a ventriculoperitoneal shunt.

articleTitle: Desing of Two Degrees of Freedom Wrist Rehabilitation Device
abstract: This paper present the design of a wrist rehabilitation device that is aimed at a patient diagnosed with Hereditary Angioedema (HAE), a condition that does not allow an effective recuperation from a wrist injury. First determine the conditions that the device must perform in order to determine the mechanism used to obtain the two movement type necessary, Flexion-Extension and Adduction-Abduction, to then adapt the different elements that allow to comply with the rest of the design conditions. Getting a simple device whose movement is generated by 2 servomotors that in which program angle, speed and time, conditions established by specialist to generate rehabilitation routines to the patient. The activity whit the device is performed in an autonomous way which helps the patient because the condition of HAE makes necessary that a constant rehabilitation be carried out daily.

articleTitle: Analysis of Auto-Reclosing Options in Venezuelan 765 kV System Including Series Compensation
abstract: This article shows an analysis of auto-reclosing options for Venezuelan 765 kV transmission system, considering the future inclusion of series compensation. Six transmission lines will have series compensation. Single-phase reclosing option is only analyzed for the four transmission lines which already have neutral grounding reactors, since these reactors are necessary for the success of single-phase reclosing action. Three-phase reclosing option is analyzed for the remaining two transmission lines which will have series compensation. New transmission limits, due to the use of analyzed reclosing options, are found by using a power system stability software, and it is shown that the increment of these limits is significant. In case of non-successful reclosure when the power transfer is near to the transmission limit, an automatic load-shedding is recommended to avoid the power system instability. A general summary about series compensation and auto-reclosure in transmission systems is included in this article for the sake of clearness.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of and Induction Motor with Optimized Harmonic Distortion
abstract: This paper shows the development of a sensorless control for the induction motor, using a three-phase multilevel converter of 15 steps per line with optimization of the first 50 harmonics, based on a law voltage vs. frequency, implanted in a single source H-bridge multilevel converter with control based on an FPGA Virtex 5, the sensorless control allows to close the speed control loop with the current measurements, eliminating the need to use mechanically coupled sensors. The experimental tests presented in the work allow validating the THD optimization in the whole frequency range, the adequate behavior of the common source multilevel converter as adjust speed device and the proper functioning of the sensorless control.

articleTitle: Selection of Renewable Energies in Urban Environments by Applying the Fahp Method, Case Study: City of Cuenca Universidad PolitéCnica Salesiana
abstract: The following research presents a multicriteria methodology for the selection of renewable energies in urban environments of the city of Cuenca. Particularly, it focuses on those technologies that use city resources that can be used to produce electricity. Multicriteria decision-making techniques are used as a support tool. We use the Hierarchical Analytical Process with the application of fuzzy logic. This method is widely used within the selection process, and mostly in energy planning. The purpose of fuzzy logic is to decrease the inaccuracy of the AHP method, thus resolving the vagueness of the judgments delivered by the decision makers.

articleTitle: Economic Model to Determine Electric Car Price Through Incentives
abstract: Environment protection will always be a concern of all world societies. Automotive fleet after the industry is responsible of greenhouse gases emission. The United States, Norway, Sweden, China, France and other countries, a few years ago have begun their migration process to Electric Vehicles, however, there are barriers that do not allow to accelerate their deployment, especially their prices and infrastructure lack for their charge. The study goal is to analyze incentives impact over vehicle final price. Scenarios probabilities of taxes reduction, granting of subsidies, among other benefits are proposed and the best conditions are evaluated. The results showed that the best scenarios are given with taxes reduction approximately in 20%. Bond subsidy also contribute an average of 10%.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of a Pharmacodynamic and Pharmacokinetics (PK/PD) Model for Application in General Anesthesia
abstract: In the application of general anesthesia, the implementations of pharmacokinetic /pharmacodynamics models (PK / PD) are a very useful tool for making decisions and analysis. These models allow us to know the behavior over time of the drug and its effect on the human body, either in an instant or in a predictive way. In this research, we built an implementation of the model PK / PD proposed by Minto for Remifentanil on an FPGA. The FPGA as an innovative and disruptive technology of the biomedical industry presents attractive features such as reprogrammability, security and control of data and execution times, fast processing, scalability, as they are described in hardware. For the solution of the Minto's PK/PD model, the numerical method fourth order Runge-Kutta was chosen. A preliminary design was made in MATLAB and compared with the ODE45 (ordinary differential equation) library of the same platform to verify the validity of the algorithm. The hardware description was made in the Quartus software in VHDL and it was implemented on an Altera DE0- Nano kit. The tests were made using Simulink's FPGA-in-the-loop strategy. The results showed that it is possible to implement this type of models on FPGAs without using special functions, with an MSE error of 4.4548×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> approximately, almost negligible, between the result delivered by MATLAB and the one obtained through the implementation on the Altera.

articleTitle: Design of a Phantom for the Validation of a Method Based in Color Doppler to Compare Fluids in Two Sections of a Blood Vessel
abstract: The blood flow behavior in the ophthalmic artery (OA) shows measurable variability with relation to neuropathological events. In the same way, the intra-cranial pressure (ICP) is a good indicator to assess the circulatory system in the brain, however it is not easy to get a quantitative value from noninvasive techniques. Recently, a study presents a method to determine the ICP comparing the speed curves of two different segments on the ophthalmic artery. Even though, there is not a system to emulate the ophtalmic artery in order to test the ICP measurement method. This paper proposes the design of a standard instrument (phantom) with hydraulic and pneumatic components to evaluate the correlation between two Color Doppler speed measures that come from two different pipelines, representing blood vessels. Furthermore, a controlled pressure system is introduced to handle the conditions of one of the vessels in order to achieve a similar behavior among both vessels.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Generation Projects with Renewable Energy Resources, via Tax Stimuli. Case Study with Colombian 1715 Law
abstract: Energy generation projects may be achievable insofar as they guarantee their technical and economic feasibility. Currently, there is a notable increase in installed electrical capacity with Renewable Energy, and furthermore, several countries now have experiment the diversification of their energy mix, so they deal with future challenges associated with their energy model. Therefore, authors of this technical contribution present a practical study case related to realization of energy projects, specifically, cogeneration projects with photovoltaic solar energy. This leads to demonstration of the relevance of stimulus energy policies through tax benefits, given the fact that it allows feasibility of these kind of projects. The study is presented with an application of Law 1715 issued by the Congress of Colombia, whose purpose is to motivate the investment in generation projects with renewable energy resources.

articleTitle: Technical-Economical Study for Solar Power Generation at USTA's Main Campus
abstract: The article deals with a technical-economic study to establish the viability of taking advantage of solar energy in the main USTA Bucaramanga campus comparing deployment costs for 2011 and 2018 at the light of recent changes in regulatory policies. The cost for its implementation and use based on an estimated consumption is analyzed. The comparison of power consumption against the costs of implementing a system based on photovoltaic panels showed that the initial cost has lowered over the years reducing the equilibrium point. In this case, this is true if all the available for power generation area is used regardless if the power is consumed on site or sell back to the electric company.

articleTitle: Impacts of Demand Response Under Wind Power Uncertainty in Network-Constrained Electricity Markets
abstract: Large amounts of renewable generation are participating into network-constrained electricity networks. The uncertainty and volatility associated to renewable resources are imposing new challenges for power system operation. Additionally, the integration of demand response resources represent a new challenge, creating new complexities in the power system operation. The operation decisions in power markets use a combined optimal power flow and unit commitment to dispatch economically generation units under security restrictions. This paper constructs a model to include demand response in the optimal power flow under wind power uncertainty. The model is formulated as a mixed-integer linear quadratic problem and evaluated through Monte-Carlo simulations. The uncertainty in wind power forecasting is captured by a large number of scenarios around a trajectory bid by the wind power generator. The proposed model is tested on the standard IEEE 39-bus system including numerical results that show substantial benefits.

articleTitle: System of Communication, Modeling and Simulation of the Radar System at the Mariscal Lamar Airport in the City of Cuenca-Ecuador
abstract: In this article we present the modeling and simulation in MATLAB of the radar system under different conditions and characteristic parameters in the Airport Corporation of Cuenca, the company in charge of administering the Mariscal la Mar Airport dedicated to providing airport services. The radar system is responsible for monitoring the transit of aircraft in the airspace, a system that provides security, order and provide pilots with instructions and necessary information within the airspace of their jurisdiction, with the aim of preventing collisions, mainly between aircraft and obstacles in the maneuvering area.

articleTitle: Non-Linear Iterative Regularization Algorithm for Neural Activity Reconstruction from EEG Data
abstract: In this work a novel non-linear iterative regularization algorithm applied to the reconstruction of neuronal activity is presented. A physiologically-based non-linear spatio-temporal constraint is used for solving the dynamic inverse problem associated to the reconstruction of neural activity of the distributed sources. The proposed method includes the spatio-temporal constraint in a cost function based on a l -2 norm. A simulated EEG data-set is used in order to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm for three and five simultaneously active sources under several signal-to-noise ratios, by using relative error measurement. A comparison analysis is performed against the MSP and IRA-L2 source reconstruction methods, where the proposed non-linear method improves the reconstruction of neural activity in terms of the relative error.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Phalanges Based on Iteration of a Prosthesis
abstract: In this work an electromechanical hand is implemented based on the study and implementation of the phalanges of the five fingers of the hand, a control system based on a microcontroller was implemented that takes as feedback signals coming from flexosensors and strain gauges. The movement of the fingers was made based on myoelectric signals in real time, these signals were acquired through an innovative method of acquisition based on patterns. The tests performed were measurements with extended hand, closed hand and pressing an object that validates the present proposal.

articleTitle: Development of a Boost Power Factor Correction Converter with 95% Efficiency
abstract: This work presents the design and construction of a Boost Power Factor Correction (PFC) Converter that reduced Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the input current waveform from a Switched Mode Power Supply (SMPS), synchronized the input voltage and input current waveforms such that the Power Factor (PF) delivered to the mains was corrected almost to unity. This device is a power converter of size 14.2x16.3x17cm, that uses isolation elements for reducing common and differential noise, the PFC ICE3PCS01, driver 1EDI60N12AF and the CoolMOS IPZ65R045C7. The converter supplied a 1.2 kW nominal power to a resistive load and achieved 95% of efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\eta)$</tex> for a 122 Vrms input voltage.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Signal Specific Spectrum Sensing Techniques for WRANs
abstract: This work presents hardware implementation of 4 Spectrum Sensing (SS) techniques for ATSC/A53 TV signals, defined in the IEEE 802.22 standard. The implemented techniques are: Field Sync Correlation Detector (FSCD), Segment-Sync Autocorrelation Detector (SSAD), Spectral Correlation (SC), and Pilot Sensing (PS). FSCD and SSAD use the synchronization information in the ATSC signal to measure the occupancy of the channel; and SC and PS are based on the spectral features of the ATSC signal. The 4 techniques were implemented on an FPGA and their performance was checked using an ATSC signal captured in field. Both FSCD and SSAD detect ATSC signals with Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs) above -14.5 dB; SC detects ATSC signals with SNRs above -25 dB; and PS detects ATSC signals with SNRS above -33 dB.

articleTitle: A Method for Steady State Analysis of Doubly Fed Induction Generator
abstract: This paper present a methodology for the steady state analysis of Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) considering the operation areas of wind turbine. First, using the spatial vector method, the steady state dq model of DFIG, is deduced. Then the operation zones are defined, based on electrical and mechanical restrictions. From the wind speed, the turbine torque and the speed is calculated, then with these two variables and the assigned power factor the other variables of DFIG are defined using the steady state dq model. Finally, the simulation and results analysis of operation are carried out for different power factors.

articleTitle: Developing a Prototype for Remote Viewing of Telescope Images Using Mobile Devices
abstract: This document describes the development of a prototype to share a series of images captured from the eyepiece of a telescope in activities of scientific dissemination in an astronomical observatory. The developed prototype includes the use of a smartphone for capturing images and another mobile device as receiving equipment; streaming protocols are used to improve the use of a WiFi network during the transmission of images, reaching reasonable results in the reception of astronomical images. To attach the smartphone to the telescopes several prototypes of fixing systems or adapter were developed, generating a whole learning process in which finally a rapid prototyping technique was used to build a stable but flexible base element in order to enable the adaptation of the device to a set of different patterns of capturing images, in case of this could be necessary. Some developed tests made it possible to identify potential problems of the communication scheme of the selected Wi-Fi network, so that a redesign of the communications patterns was generated taking advantage of the configuration features of the smartphones used in the solution.

articleTitle: Development of a Robotic Lower-Limb Exoskeleton for Gait Rehabilitation: AGoRA Exoskeleton
abstract: Stroke significantly affects millions of individuals around the world every year, leading to considerable physical impairment and serious long-term disability. Gait is one of the most important daily-life activities affected in stroke victims. The development of an ambulatory lower-limb exoskeleton intended for use in stroke survivors is presented in this paper. It is envisioned as an actuated device in the sagittal plane, capable of producing the necessary torque to move the hip, knee and ankle joints (this latter by means of a variable-stiffness ankle-foot orthosis). An additional passive add/abduction degree of freedom at the hip joint is included, as a way to improve walking balance. A control approach for the actuated joints, which aims to assist the subject only when needed, is also proposed. The main goal of this assistive device is to promote the early incorporation of stroke patients with mobility impairments to a feasible rehabilitation treatment. Such device opens the possibility to study means that might optimize conventional rehabilitation treatment.

articleTitle: Development of an Interface for Human-Robot Interaction on a Robotic Platform for Gait Assistance: AGoRA Smart Walker
abstract: Alterations to the human locomotor system, commonly result in problems related to balance and gait stability. To address such gait dysfunctions, several mobility aids have been developed. Devices, such as Smart Walkers (SWs), in conjunction with Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) interfaces, are typically implemented. However, common HRI interfaces are not able to provide safe assistance, at the same time as, proper environment interaction and natural user interaction. In this paper is presented the implementation of a safety robust and novel HRI interface on a SW, that provides secure human-walker interaction, as well as, environment and user interaction systems. To this end, a navigation system, a people detection system, a gait cadence estimator, a user's intention detection system and several control strategies were implemented. Additionally, a preliminary validation was conducted with a healthy user.

articleTitle: SVM-Based System for Broken Rotor Bar Detection in Induction Motors
abstract: In this paper we propose a system for the detection of broken bars (BB) in induction motors (IM) based on a binary SVM classifier. Statistical features obtained from a IM current are used as inputs of the classifier. We train the classifier with simulation data, using a qd model of IM. Through simulation, 360 records of 120 cycles were generated in which different IM conditions were considered, healthy, rotor fault and disturbances in torque and voltage. Finally, the classifier was validated with experimental laboratory data, obtained from an IM of 5.5 kW in healthy, 2 and 3 BB, with different load and supply voltage conditions. The results show that the proposed classifier allows detection with 91.67% accuracy, and without false negatives (faulty IMs classified as heathy).

articleTitle: Control Strategy for Oil Production Wells with Electrical Submersible Pumping Based on the Nonlinear Model-Based Predictive Control Technique
abstract: This paper presents a control strategy for the optimization of artificial lift systems (ALS) with electrical submersible pumping (ESP), executing a nonlinear model-based predictive control (NMPC) to manipulate the operating frequency of the pump and control the flow rate through the well, including specific restrictions over the system and considering its present and future behavior. The controller was designed according to a practical approach, considering the field implementation limitations and requirements. It provides significant efficiency and safety features, maximizing the revenue and operating the system in the optimal range, while respecting the system constraints and taking into account its predicted behavior. The control proposal includes the system modelling and its dynamic identification, the design of the NMPC controller, and its configuration and tuning in a simulation environment. The results of the simulation of the control system performance for an existing well are shown.

articleTitle: Viability Assessment of a Real-Time Simulation Model for a Residential DC Microgrid Network to Compensate Electricity Disturbances in Puerto Rico
abstract: With the passing of hurricanes María and Irma, the island of Puerto Rico was left devastated. This disaster left the electric grid de-energized and millions of people, schools, and hospitals without power. The extended blackout demonstrated a need for energy alternatives that supply power during times of crisis when traditional electricity is not readily available. A system that makes use of renewable energy generation, battery storage and electric vehicle integration can be a feasible alternative during periods when the utility cannot successfully supply power to consumers. In addition, excess power can be supplied to neighboring microgrids. Real-time (RT) simulation tools can demonstrate dynamic operations of these systems. This paper presents a RT simulation model that emulates residential electrification through a microgrid. This dynamic model is a planning tool for microgrid power systems to select designs capable of operation during months-long blackouts.

articleTitle: Step-by-Step Kinematic Modeling and Control of a Robot with a Free-Floating Base
abstract: Motion generation for legged mobile robots, which are characterized by an underactuated free-floating base, has become an important research topic in recent years. Although several research groups have addressed the problem of controlling the base in their own implementations, there is no work that completely describes the framework used to handle it, which makes it complicated for new researchers to find a proper solution. This paper aims at bridging this gap and presents a step-by-step guide to model the effect of the floating base on the kinematics of the robot, and to properly control it to achieve whole-body motion. The proposed framework is generic and can be applied to any legged underactuated robot such as a humanoid robot, a quadruped, an hexapod, amongst others. The results show an example of implementation using the model of a quadruped robot.

articleTitle: Towards a Sustainable Energy-Efficient Future at Universities, Universidad San Francisco de Quito Case Study, Phase I
abstract: This paper explores the building commissioning process required for improving energy consumption on campus facilities building a dynamic model that considers the principles of energy efficiency proposed by the Intergovernmental Panel for Climate Change. First, the model of the energy efficiency program adopted by the University under study is described. Then, the results obtained from the initial energy evaluation phase are presented; this process consisted on understanding the patterns of energy consumption, obtained by analyzing electrical load profiles from key measurement points around campus facilities during periods of normal operation and holidays, as well as maintenance and behavioral patterns that fit this consumption. Finally, the initial actions taken in equipment and maintenance, the suggested changes in user behavior and the energy savings obtained as result of the changes implemented are also reported and analyzed. Early results obtained indicate that a sustainable energy-efficient policy is feasible.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective N:1 Firewall Array Via Subnet-Levcl Load Balancing by SDN/OpenFlow Switches
abstract: Enterprise networks' firewalls are rarely set up in a shared-protection (N:1) configuration, preferring instead the more costly active-stand by (1+1) configuration. This is due to, in part, to the high cost associated with software-based per-flow load balancing at high traffic loads. In this work, we propose the use of SDN/OpenFlow switches as a low-cost hardware-based alternative for subnet-level load balancing, for use in a N:1 firewall array. Our design guarantees that the N:1 system exhibits the same performance of a 1+1 system but at a much lower cost. In particular, the design provides lossless firewall handover of subnets in response to traffic bursts. A prototype of the system has been implemented in Python over the base of the Floodlight OpenFlow Controller and tested in our SDN Test-Bed using the ISPDSL II traffic traces, evaluating the behavior during traffic peaks. Initial results show that the system successfully migrate subnet traffic without packet losses, call blockings, or TCAM exhaustion.

articleTitle: A Convex Optimization Model for Bidirectional Vehicle-To-Grid Operation
abstract: Global warming is one of the environmental reasons for the adoption of the electric vehicle (VE). This technology is very welcome by society but carries great challenges to electricity distribution networks. VEs will need to be recharged and extra amount power demand could lead to occurrence of several operational problems in the distribution system. An optimization model is required in a concept called vehicle-to-grid or V2G. The main issue of this optimization model lies in the power flow equation which are non-linear and non-convex making the problem hard to be solved for large scale integration of VEs. Therefore, we use a semidefinite approximation of the power flow and evaluate the model in different scenarios. Electric vehicles are coordinated by aggragators that are spatially distributed along a primary feeder. Each aggregator collects a group of EVs of different rate of charger. The objective function is to minimize power loss and maximize state-of-charge (SOC) or owner satisfaction. Several scenarios were taken into account: first, a base case where we compare the proposed model with others models propose in the literature, next we analyze the integration of EVs for 25%, 50%,75% and 100% of the total power demand of the system, with of aim of evaluating the control variables and load loadability on the IEEE 37 nodes and IEEE 29 nodes test feeders.

articleTitle: The EGTS: When the Aerospace Ecosystem is not Ready
abstract: Commercial aviation is considered by many as one of the most innovative environments due to its dynamism, competitiveness, and technology applied. In this context, aerospace manufacturers seek for optimizing in every single phase of flight the slightest advantadge to create in it, a new market niche. This paper presents one perspective of the promising project known as electric green taxiing system (EGTS) presented by Honeywell and Safran, its features, its motivations, as well as some variables that were not initially included and played a significant role in the outcome. Likewise, organizational framework that supports a novel product or process represents a key factor in its furthuer implementation. This paper suggests that despite having all ingredients to become a succesful product, other factors are decisive in its implementation.
